rules.statement: Validate every JWT a provider issues (ID token, logout token, signed UserInfo) through one shared validation core that owns algorithm policy, key resolution, decryption, replicated-issuer check and failure wording; each token kind checks only its own claims.
rules.why: The surrounding work is the same for every kind, so it must exist once and a fix to it reaches every kind.
rules.check: Look for a token-kind validator that builds its own algorithm allow-list, decrypts, resolves keys or words generic failures itself instead of calling the shared core with a profile.

rules.statement: Validate a received JWT under an explicit signature-algorithm allow-list that permits only asymmetric algorithms (never `none`), is intersected with the registered list and the provider's advertised list when present, fails when the result is empty, and is passed as `ValidSignatureAlgorithms` so the header is checked before any cryptography runs.
rules.why: An allow-list keeps `none` and unregistered algorithms out, and checking the header first avoids running cryptography on a disallowed token.
rules.check: Check JWT validation setup for missing `ValidSignatureAlgorithms`, symmetric or `none` algorithms permitted, no intersection with registration/metadata, or an empty result that does not fail.

rules.statement: Treat an empty or null algorithm allow-list as permitting nothing, never as permitting every algorithm.
rules.why: The conventions use explicit allow-lists; a null list that permits everything was rejected.
rules.check: Look for code that skips the algorithm filter or permits all algorithms when a configured list is null or empty.

rules.statement: When decrypting a provider-issued JWE, permit only the registered asymmetric key-management algorithms (RSA-OAEP*, ECDH-ES*) and registered content-encryption algorithms, never `RSA1_5`, `dir`, AES key wrap or PBES2, and permit no compression (`ValidCompressionAlgorithms = []`).
rules.why: RFC 8725 §3.2 and §3.6 forbid RSA1_5 and compression; the provider encrypts only to a public key the client published, so shared-key algorithms have no place.
rules.check: Inspect decryption policy for RSA1_5, dir, A*KW, PBES2 or non-empty compression algorithms being allowed, or unregistered enc values.

rules.statement: Derive a client's permitted token encryption algorithms only from its registration, never from the provider's `*_encryption_*_values_supported` metadata.
rules.why: The registration fixes the values, so the provider's list adds nothing the client can trust more.
rules.check: Look for decryption policy code reading provider discovery encryption metadata.

rules.statement: Make token encryption all or nothing: when the client registered encryption, reject a plain JWS with `invalid_token`; when it registered none, reject a JWE with `algorithm_not_permitted`.
rules.why: Accepting an unencrypted token when encryption is registered is a downgrade that lets an attacker who cannot encrypt to the client substitute a plain token.
rules.check: Check that the validator verifies the received token was a JWE when encryption is registered and refuses a JWE otherwise.

rules.statement: When a JWE header replicates `iss` (RFC 7519 §5.3), require it to be a string equal to the expected issuer, or fail with `invalid_issuer`.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout §2.4 and RFC 7519 §5.3 let the header replicate claims, and a mismatch must not be ignored.
rules.check: Look for JWE handling that ignores a header `iss` or accepts a non-string or mismatched value.

rules.statement: Use only the client's own asymmetric keys, carrying `use` `enc`, as JWE decryption keys, and throw `InvalidOperationException` when encryption is registered but no decryption key ring is configured.
rules.why: The client decrypts with its own private keys held in its key ring; a missing key ring is a configuration error.
rules.check: Check decryption key selection for symmetric keys, keys without `use` `enc`, or silent fallback when no key ring exists.

rules.statement: Throw `InvalidOperationException` for inconsistent token-encryption configuration, such as content-encryption algorithms set without key-management algorithms.
rules.why: Such a combination is a configuration error, not a token validation failure.
rules.check: Look for configuration combinations that are silently accepted or reported as a token failure.

rules.statement: Never include the token in validation failure text: use fixed messages for decryption and signature failures, and otherwise only the underlying error message.
rules.why: Failure text must not leak the token.
rules.check: Look for failure reasons, exceptions or logs that interpolate the raw token string.

rules.statement: Tell a decryption failure (`decryption_failed`) from a signature failure (`invalid_signature`) by whether the JWT validator had already asked for signing keys when it threw, not by parsing the token a second time.
rules.why: Signing keys are resolved only for the enclosed JWS after decryption, so the validator already shows whether decryption succeeded; parsing first duplicates its work.
rules.check: Look for code that pre-parses a token to classify failures, or that maps every decode or key-not-found exception to one code.

rules.statement: Run token validation in a fixed order (algorithm policy, then decrypt, signature, issuer, audience, lifetime, then the encryption requirement, replicated `iss` and `typ`, then claim checks), and record a logout token's `jti` for replay detection only after every other check passes.
rules.why: A token that fails any other check must never record its `jti`.
rules.check: Check that the replay store write happens last and that no check is moved before the algorithm policy.

rules.statement: When a JWT's `kid` is not found among the provider's keys, trigger at most one rate-limited key set refresh; without a `kid`, try every key filtered by `use` and `alg`.
rules.why: Limiting refreshes handles key rotation without letting tokens force unbounded fetches.
rules.check: Look for key resolution that refreshes on every miss, without rate limiting, or that ignores `use`/`alg` when no `kid` is present.

rules.statement: During token validation, let cancellation propagate, and rethrow provider failures as provider exceptions instead of turning them into token validation failures.
rules.why: A provider failure or cancellation is not a property of the token.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks that swallow `OperationCanceledException` or turn provider errors into invalid-token results.
